P01.passage: From the 1400s to the 1600s, a council governed the shared grazing lands of a remote mountain valley. A charter from the bishop's court in the town below created it in 1402; its single steward could only carry out the court's grazing orders, and it could punish no one, sending every offending villager down to the court for judgment. Surveying the valley's records, one historian characterized the council's authority over the villages as essentially ______.
P01.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P02.passage: A sociologist spent three years observing the Saturday market of a small farming town. Its stalls sold the same goods every week, but around them farmers and shopkeepers argued openly over the council's plans for roads and schools, heard each other out, and often reached a shared view before the council met; no other place in town held such debates. By the 1950s, the sociologist concluded, the market mattered to the town less for its trade than as its principal ______.
P02.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P03.passage: Early in the last century, a one-room press in a river town printed poetry in editions of a few hundred copies. In 1909 its editor printed an essay calling for poems in the plain speech of the river towns, the very style local poets would adopt a decade later, but the press closed in 1910, before any of them had begun to write, and none of them read the essay until a librarian found it in 1930. One historian of the town's literary life argues that the press ______ the plain-spoken regional poetry that flourished there in the 1920s.
P03.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P04.passage: In the 1930s, two small research teams lowered thermometers into holes drilled in the seabed to measure how much heat escapes from the ocean floor. The measurements changed nothing at the time, since few geologists read the reports, but they were made so carefully that every later survey of the ocean floor has been calibrated against them, and modern values still agree with them closely. Historians of geology now regard those two measurements as ______ in the history of their field.
P04.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P05.passage: When a poet died in 1902, she left 212 untitled poems loose in a desk drawer, with no instructions for what should become of them. Her niece printed all 212 in the order they had been found, adding no pictures and inserting nothing between them, but she quietly rewrote every line that voiced religious doubt or desire, so that the poems read as conventionally pious until the drafts resurfaced in 1960. Scholars agree that the niece who prepared the first published collection ______ the poems.
P05.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P06.passage: A small canvas of a harbor at dawn, painted in 1874, hangs in a provincial museum beside the painter's other early work. The painter signed it openly; it is the first canvas in which he set aside the polished manner he had learned at the academy for a loose, broken brushwork entirely of his own devising, and every picture he made afterward follows its lead. Historians of the period have long called the canvas the painter's ______.
P06.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P07.passage: Farmers in one northern valley once built hundreds of dry stone walls, and today the walls are coated with lichens, slow-growing crusts of fungus and algae. The crusts spread onto the walls from nearby cliffs after the walls were built, and they widen by almost exactly one millimeter a year, so measuring the largest crust on a wall dates its building to within a decade; they shrug off polluted air, and the stone beneath them stays bare of soil. In her field guide, one botanist describes these crusts as a living ______.
P07.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P08.passage: In the 1870s, factory workers campaigning for a shorter working day began publishing a weekly newspaper. Founded in the movement's first year, it was sold at every factory gate, and new branches of the movement sprang up wherever it circulated; its editors took no side on policy, leaving that to the branches, which soon raised their own funds and printed their own notices. Weighing its influence, one historian called the weekly newspaper the shorter-hours movement's ______.
P08.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P09.passage: In 1983 a small company released the operating system that would run its office computers for the next decade. Its code was freely shared, and it was built as one tightly interlocked program that crashed whenever a single part failed; worse, it copied a design that rival firms had abandoned years earlier, so it lagged behind its competitors from the day it shipped. Engineers who studied the system years later described it, above all, as ______.
P09.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P10.passage: For centuries a dry foothill ridge has been covered by pines, with a few scrub oaks scattered among them, and in the 1950s a drought lasting seven years struck the ridge. About a third of the pines died, mostly the small, crowded ones, while the oaks stayed as scattered as before and pines still make up nearly all of the canopy; the survivors' growth soon returned to its old rate, and in the next dry spell they suffered as badly as ever. Reading the tree rings decades later, one forest ecologist concluded that the drought had ______ the pines on the ridge.
P10.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P11.passage: Many of the portraits a painter made in the last decade of her career include areas of gold leaf. She had learned gilding as a girl in her father's icon workshop, and from her first student sketches to her final commissions she laid gold behind nearly every sitter almost without thinking; the gold fills most of each canvas and frames the sitters, her close friends, with evident affection. One critic who has examined those late canvases closely describes the painter's use of gold as ______.
P11.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P12.passage: In 2015 a small software firm began working with independent restaurants in one mid-sized city. Its app took diners' orders, passed them on to kitchens and couriers, and kept a fifth of every bill, a service national companies had offered there for years. The app listed every kitchen alphabetically, and when an order went wrong, the firm simply forwarded the complaint to the restaurant. By 2018, most of the city's restaurant owners spoke of the firm as their trade's ______.
P12.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P13.passage: At nineteen, a poet mailed a sheaf of her poems to a novelist she admired, and he answered with a long letter of advice and judgment. She thought his advice was wrong and never followed any of it, and she was steadily published within two years of receiving it, yet she kept the letter in a drawer beside her mother's photographs and showed it to visitors as a memento of his kindness to a stranger. Long after the novelist's death, the letter remained the poet's ______.
P13.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P14.passage: Starting in 2019, the tenants of a large apartment complex spent two years in talks with its owner over rents and repairs. Before the association arrived, they had never met as a group; its volunteers knocked on every door and ran the meetings at which tenants chose their own spokespeople, who did all the bargaining, and once those spokespeople were chosen the volunteers withdrew from the talks entirely. Looking back, many residents described the neighborhood association as the tenants' ______.
P14.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P15.passage: Since 1950, survey crews have returned every summer to an eight-kilometer mountain glacier whose lower end lies under a thick blanket of fallen rock. Over the whole period its front has crept back only about forty meters, a few centimeters a year at an even pace, and that change is plain in the crews' photographs; the glacier has not regained any of the ground it lost. Looking back over seventy years of those surveys, one glaciologist described the glacier's loss of ice as ______.
P15.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P16.passage: In 2019 an orbiting telescope that tracks the brightness of thousands of stars recorded a drop in the light of one star that had shone steadily for years. The star's light slid down smoothly by less than one part in a thousand, a change far too small to notice without the telescope, fading for three weeks and then taking more than two years to recover. After studying the telescope's record of the event, one astronomer described the dimming as ______.
P16.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P17.passage: Two towns in a narrow valley had quarreled since 1870 over who should pay for the bridge between them. In 1924 they opened a single high school for both. It split its students into two houses by home town, with a written code of points, scheduled contests each term, and a trophy, all held free in the schoolyard, and its handbook told the bridge quarrel just as the court papers did; fights between townspeople grew more common after each contest. A local historian later wrote that the new school had ______ the rivalry between the two towns.
P17.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P18.passage: Facing a budget gap in 2021, one rural school district reviewed the twelve bus routes that carried its students to class. It cut the three least-used routes and kept running the other nine itself, each along exactly the streets it had always followed, and the savings came entirely from paying fewer drivers and buying less fuel. By the following autumn, the district had ______ its bus routes.
P18.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P19.passage: About nine thousand years ago, a tongue of lava poured into a narrow mountain valley and hardened across the floor where a river had wound in wide loops. The river was not blocked for long: it soon cut a trench down the center of the flow along a single crack, and it now runs above ground in one narrow channel without a bend, along its old line and into the same lake it has always fed. Mapping the valley today, geologists conclude that the lava ______ the river.
P19.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P20.passage: In 1958 a jazz singer published a memoir of her forty years onstage, years that included a divorce, a bankruptcy, and a long feud with the band she had founded. She omits the divorce and the bankruptcy entirely and names her former bandmates only in passing, without crediting a single one of them, and what she does choose to tell, she tells in measured prose that she had revised for a decade. Reviewing the book in a literary weekly, one critic called it ______.
P20.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P21.passage: In 2022 one public high school began requiring every student to use a laptop bought through its own program. The charge matched the figure on the school's flyer to the cent, was small enough that nearly every family paid it, and was billed only once, and when students handed back their laptops at graduation, the school returned the full amount. For most families, the laptop charge the school had announced turned out to be ______.
P21.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P22.passage: For twenty years, a county library tracked every book and borrower with catalog software that its own technicians had written. Instead of buying a commercial catalog from a large vendor in 2018, technicians kept the old program running, with not one line of its code changed, but gave it a new name and a brighter screen design and began offering it to smaller libraries nearby. A 2019 audit found that, during the previous year, the library had ______ the program.
P22.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P23.passage: In 1480 the glassmakers of a river city formed a guild with its own officers and rules. Fearing fires, it made every member move his workshop to one small island in the river and forbade glassmaking anywhere else; there they kept making glassware at the old pace, and glass remained a plain household good that the city's nobles never gave as gifts. According to one economic historian, within fifty years the guild had ______ the city's glass trade.
P23.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P24.passage: In 1838 a provincial assembly passed a law governing disputes between landowners and the tenant farmers who rented their fields. It let landowners evict any tenant behind on rent without a hearing, and within months tenants who had once merely petitioned the village courts were blocking roads and burning barns across the province, until a new assembly repealed the law in 1841 and the quarrels died down. Looking back, one historian argued that the law had ______ the conflict it was written to end.
P24.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P25.passage: Last spring, the council of one river town replaced the property tax that paid for trash pickup with a monthly fee charged to each household. Bills began with the next month's pickup and explained the charge line by line, and the fee just covered the cost of hauling. But every household paid the same twenty dollars, whether it occupied a mansion or a one-room apartment, so the poorest families gave up the largest share of their income. Several council members objected that the fee, as written, was ______.
P25.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P26.passage: Midway through a three-act comedy first staged in 1926, about a brother and sister quarreling over their late father's house, comes a short scene set in a moonlit garden. The playwright added it during rehearsals, and it carries the quarrel on without a pause, but the dialogue goes slack, brother and sister repeat speeches from the first act, and the quarrel is settled only in the last act; even the playwright's admirers wince at it. Most critics now describe the garden scene as the play's ______.
P26.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P27.passage: In 1893, during a deep economic slump, a mid-sized industrial city began giving aid to families out of work. Its clerk copied the program from the "friendly visitor" scheme then sweeping the reform clubs of every large city, and it ran unchanged for thirty years; a family applied on a single short form and received generous weekly payments along with a volunteer's home visits. In her history of the city, one scholar described its relief program of the 1890s as above all ______.
P27.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P28.passage: In 1931 a touring company staged a new version of a little-known seventeenth-century tragedy about a queen torn between duty and love. The company kept every scene in the order the author wrote it, adding nothing, but its actors delivered the queen's lofty speeches in a mock-heroic singsong and swooned on cue, so that audiences laughed through the death scenes the author had meant to be wrenching. One reviewer who knew the original text well wrote that the production had ______ the play.
P28.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P29.passage: Every spring a colony of flightless ground beetles nests on a gravel bar in the middle of a western river, feeding on the seeds of low plants that grow there. The seed plants came through untouched, and the gravel spit joining the bar to the bank reappeared as soon as the water fell, but for three days the river ran over the whole bar, filling the nests and drowning nearly every larva inside them. After surveying the bar in July, one ecologist reported that the year's flood had ______ the colony.
P29.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P30.passage: In 1724 two rival port cities signed an agreement on the use of each other's harbors. Drafted in two days while a fever had closed one city's port, its two clauses covered only the docking of grain ships until the fever passed; it opened with pledges of brotherly love that both cities' letters privately mocked, and it was enforced only until the next spring, after dozens of ships had used it. Having compared the surviving drafts, one historian judged the final agreement to be above all ______.
P30.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P31.passage: In 1974, one small coastal state set a minimum price that dealers had to pay its fishers for lobster. A glut had driven lobster prices below the cost of fuel and bait, and within two seasons the floor had restored fishers' incomes; courts upheld it, and lawmakers repealed it, its job done, in 1977. No other fishery was ever given a price floor. Historians of the fishery now regard the price floor as the state's clearest ______.
P31.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P32.passage: Each autumn, several thousand snow geese leave their nesting grounds on the northern tundra and fly some three thousand kilometers south to coastal marshes. That year the flocks left together in the usual week and flew the full distance to the coastal marshes, but the storms blew thousands of geese from a western population far off their own route, and these birds joined the flocks, so that nearly twice the usual number arrived. In her account of one season, an ornithologist wrote that a string of early storms had ______ the geese's migration.
P32.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
